facts.fact: Founded April 1896 and named for Sir Walter Scott's novel 'Waverley'; moved in 1898 to the former Luelling orchard on the east bank of the Willamette.
Pear trees from the orchard still stand left of the 10th green.
The Junior Clubhouse was the 'Trolley House' or 'Over Links' stop on the interurban Ardgour line; its back keeps the original double doors (developer, citing the club).

The Portland to Oregon City line opened in 1892 (East Side Railway), the first long-distance interurban passenger line; the company's cars wore maroon and cream, later blue and cream, then orange and cream.

current.subject: A green and white locomotive, for the club's Junior Clubhouse: once the 'Trolley House' (or 'Over Links') stop on the interurban Ardgour line across the property (developer, 2026-10-25).
current.keep: The locomotive: it stands for a real building on the course, whose back still has the stop's double doors.
current.weaknesses: Side-on and long; the shape reads as a toy train at 1x.

concepts.name: The Express, Head-On
concepts.rationale: The locomotive face on: round smokebox door, lamp, chimney, red buffer beam, green tanks with white lining. Symmetric and commanding.
concepts.symbolism: Arrival at the club, by the line that once stopped on the course.
concepts.interpretation: The stop served trolleys on an interurban line; a steam engine is the developer's existing subject, kept here.
concepts.tradeoffs: A trolley car would be the literal subject; the steam engine reads better at 32 px.

concepts.name: The Luelling Pear
concepts.rationale: A ripe pear with its leaf. The club plays on Henderson Luelling's old orchard, and its pear trees still stand by the 10th green.
references: Luelling orchard, the club's site since 1898 (fact)
concepts.symbolism: Roots: one of the oldest clubs in the West, playing on an orchard planted before it.
concepts.strengths: True, simple, beautiful; reads from across a room.
concepts.tradeoffs: A pear is gentle for a championship club.

recommendation: Concept 2. The pear is the club's own ground and history, and the cleanest icon in the Portland set.
options_intro: The Junior Clubhouse was the Trolley House, a stop on the interurban Ardgour line from the club's 'Riverside Links and Golf Junction era'. The line opened in 1892 as one of the first long-distance electric interurbans; the company's cars wore maroon and cream (later blue, then orange, with cream).

options.name: Head-On, Line Colours
options.idea: The interurban car face on, its pole up to the wire, in the maroon and cream the company's cars wore.
options.strength: The most authentic livery; reads at once as a trolley.
options.tradeoff: Maroon is new to the club's look.

options.name: Head-On, Waverley Green
options.idea: The same car in the green and white of the locomotive the club has now.
options.strength: Keeps the colours people know, with the right vehicle.
options.tradeoff: The green is ours, not the line's.

options.name: Along the Line
options.idea: Side on, green and cream, the rails laid across the turf: the line ran through the links.
options.tradeoff: A long shape; the windows are small at 1x.

options.name: Golf Junction
options.idea: A maroon-and-cream car passing a green and its pin, in a roundel.
options.strength: Trolley and golf together, the whole story in one badge.
options.tradeoff: The busiest of the five; more scene than symbol.

options.name: The Live Wire
options.idea: Only the trolley pole, its wheel on the wire, and the spark.
options.strength: Modern and unusual; strong on a hat.
options.tradeoff: Abstract: it can read as a wand before a trolley.

options_note: My pick is Head-On, Waverley Green: the right vehicle in the colours the club already uses. Line Colours if you want it true to the old cars.
